title: Early-warp batching quick notes
content:
Context:
- Quick morning scratch for the warp/micro-batching oddness seen on canary yesterday. Not a polished doc, just steps, numbers, hypotheses and immediate todos.
- Affected: small-sequence interactive traffic (<=512 tokens), high-QPS routes on dedicated instances with mixed model pool.

What I observed (summary):
- p50 latency for 256-token seqs rose ~18–22ms on canary vs baseline after the warp scheduler change (rolled last night). p95 shows smaller relative movement (~7–9ms).
- Token throughput unchanged. CPU on host shows intermittent spikes correlated with eviction churn in KV cache logs.
- Reproducer on a single pod: saw latency jump when two concurrent request patterns interleave (one long seq, one short burst).

Quick reproducer (local):
1) start local runtime with warp=2, batch-window=6ms: 
   ./bin/runtime --config examples/dummy-config.yaml --warp-scheduler warp_v2 --batch-window-ms 6
2) load model small-gpt (approx 6.8B)
3) run script that sends interleaved requests:
   python tools/load_tests/interleave_clients.py --clients 2 --pattern "short:10,short:10,long:300" --qps 60
4) collect traces: /tmp/runtime-trace.json and kernel logs (dmesg / journalctl)

Observed logs snippet (approx):
- [kv-cache] evict shard=3 keys=12 reason=partial-evict
- [warp] scheduled batch id=172 size=1 wait-ms=7
- [serve] cold-start kv-miss seq=1 token=0
- host CPU: user spikes to 78% for ~120ms on eviction events

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Warp scheduler sometimes forms very small batches (size=1) when interleaving long/short patterns; this defeats prefix caching and causes frequent KV cache evictions -> higher latency.
2) Batch-window tuning interacts poorly with our eviction policy: small batch-window (6ms) reduces batching but increases eviction churn for multi-tenant memory pressure.
3) A timing bug in warp_v2 where the scheduler aggressively cancels a pending batch when a long request arrives, causing two sequential cache misses instead of a merged prefix.

Quick experiments to run (short-term):
- EXP-A: Increase batch-window to 10ms on canary (warp_v2) and measure p50/p95 for short seqs. Hypothesis: slightly larger window will amortize short requests into small batches and reduce evictions.
- EXP-B: Add a cheap cooldown for eviction decisions: if last eviction < 50ms, skip non-critical evictions. Prototype flag: --eviction-cooldown-ms=50.
- EXP-C: Force warp_v2 to prefer coalescing if an existing pending batch has prefix tokens cached (cheap check). Toggle via debug flag.
- EXP-D: Run isolated single-tenant test (same QPS) to confirm whether multi-tenant mixing is necessary for the regression.

Commands to run metrics quickly (placeholders):
- collect p50/p95: python tools/metrics/aggregator.py --from 2026-03-12T06:00 --to 2026-03-12T10:00 --route small-interactive --metric latency_p50,latency_p95
- flamegraph kernel: sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 30; sudo perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl | flamegraph.pl > /tmp/flame.svg

Immediate short todos (what I will do today):
- [ ] Run EXP-A on canary-3 during low traffic window (09:30–10:00 PST). I will tag logs with canary:warp-A.
- [ ] Add quick metric to trace prefix-cache hit rate per batch in runtime (low-cost counter) and ship as debug build. PR target: small change to batcher stats. (Assign to me)
- [ ] Reproduce locally with python interleave script and capture KV cache trace (assign to Diego for deep kernel correlation).
- [ ] Post brief in #inference-runtime summarizing regression and planned experiments (link to this doc).

Notes to self / implementation sketch for EXP-B (eviction cooldown):
- Add eviction timestamp per shard (atomic u64). On eviction request check now - last_eviction < cooldown_ms -> skip non-critical eviction. This avoids burst thrash from many micro-batches.
- Cheap guard: only apply cooldown when memory pressure < 85% to avoid making pressure worse.
- Metrics to add: evictions_skipped_count, eviction_cooldown_hit_ratio.

Open questions / risks:
- Could cooldown simply move evictions later and cause one big eviction with larger pause? Need to quantify tail behavior.
- Does increasing batch-window increase client-side tail due to head-of-line blocking for long sequences? Need to measure mixed traffic shape.
- Is warp_v2 the right long-term path or do we revert to warp_v1 until we have prefix-aware coalescing?

Relevant links and quick refs:
- local repro script: tools/load_tests/interleave_clients.py
- PR (recent warp change): github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/891
- JIRA: JIRA-ENG-2147
- Slack thread: #inference-runtime yesterday 18:12 — @priya posted traces

Post-mortem sketch (if EXP-A fixes):
- Timeline: roll warp_v2 -> increase batch-window -> measure -> revert if p50 worsens for long sequences.
- If EXP-A reduces p50 and evictions_skipped_count drops, schedule a follow-up to implement prefix-aware coalescing properly rather than relying on larger windows.

Random notes (noisy):
- Consider adding a small grace for KV read reuse: if next request targets same model shard within 8ms, mark for eager merge.
- Check kernel pagecache activity during eviction windows — maybe pagecache thrash is amplifying const CPU spikes.

Next actions after morning:
- Create tiny debug PR to add batcher counters (target 2 hours).
- Run EXP-A and capture 1 hour of traffic; if improvement >= 10% p50 for short seqs -> proceed to canary ramp.
- Sync with Priya 11:30 to decide on rollback vs continue experimentation.

-- Avery
